chEn: Unit 1B · Rational Functions, End Behavior, Asymptotes & Binomial Theorem
chAr: الوحدة 1B · الدوال النسبية وسلوك الأطراف وخطوط التقارب ونظرية ذات الحدين
f: Definition 1B.1 — Rational Function Asymptotes, Removable Holes & Oblique Quotients
f_ar: Definition 1B.1 — Rational Function Asymptotes, Removable Holes & Oblique Quotients
b: For a rational function \( r(x) = \frac{P(x)}{Q(x)} \): if a factor \( (x - c)^m \) appears in both \( P \) and \( Q \) with at least as high multiplicity in \( P \), then \( x = c \) is a removable discontinuity (hole); otherwise \( x = c \) is a vertical asymptote. When \( \deg(P) = \deg(Q) + 1 \), polynomial division \( P(x) = (mx + b)Q(x) + R(x) \) yields the slant (oblique) asymptote \( y = mx + b \).
b_ar: For a rational function \( r(x) = \frac{P(x)}{Q(x)} \): if a factor \( (x - c)^m \) appears in both \( P \) and \( Q \) with at least as high multiplicity in \( P \), then \( x = c \) is a removable discontinuity (hole); otherwise \( x = c \) is a vertical asymptote. When \( \deg(P) = \deg(Q) + 1 \), polynomial division \( P(x) = (mx + b)Q(x) + R(x) \) yields the slant (oblique) asymptote \( y = mx + b \).

chEn: Unit 2B · Logarithmic Modeling, Semi-Log Plots, Inverse & Competing Functions
chAr: الوحدة 2B · النمذجة اللوغاريتمية والتمثيل شبه اللوغاريتمي والدوال العكسية
f: Definition 2B.1 — Semi-Log Plots & Residual Analysis for Exponential Models
f_ar: Definition 2B.1 — Semi-Log Plots & Residual Analysis for Exponential Models
b: If a dataset \( (x_i, y_i) \) follows an exponential model \( y = a \cdot b^x \) (\( a > 0, b > 0 \)), taking logs gives \[ \ln y = (\ln b)x + \ln a, \] so the semi-log plot \( (x, \ln y) \) is linear with slope \( \ln b \) and vertical intercept \( \ln a \). A model is appropriate when its residual plot \( r_i = y_i - \hat{y}_i \) displays random scatter around zero with no curved pattern.

chEn: Unit 3B · Sinusoidal Regression, Inverse Trig, Tangent & Polar Conics
chAr: الوحدة 3B · الانحدار الجيبي والدوال المثلثية العكسية والدوال القطبية
f: Definition 3B.1 — Sinusoidal Parameter Extraction & Polar-Cartesian Conversion
f_ar: Definition 3B.1 — Sinusoidal Parameter Extraction & Polar-Cartesian Conversion
b: For a periodic phenomenon oscillating between maximum \( M \) and minimum \( m \) with period \( P \), the sinusoidal model \( f(t) = A\cos\!\left(\frac{2\pi}{P}(t - t_{\max})\right) + D \) has amplitude \( A = \frac{M - m}{2} \) and midline \( D = \frac{M + m}{2} \). In polar coordinates \( (r, \theta) \), \( x = r\cos\theta \), \( y = r\sin\theta \), and \( r^2 = x^2 + y^2 \).
